intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the dancing lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The signature experience includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask. Steam caves and a sauna enhance the relaxation while surrounded by dramatic lava fields.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers, offering a more intimate and local hot spring experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and colorful old harbor district.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Snuba Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Drift through the crystal-clear glacial waters of Silfra, the crack between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. With visibility exceeding 100 meters, this UNESCO World Heritage site offers a surreal underwater experience. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus (Strætó) shuttle to Reykjavík. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a short orientation walk along the nearby coastline to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Reykjavík for a first evening stroll. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior viewing) and walk Laugavegur street. Check the aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) and if activity is KP-2 or higher, head to a dark coastal area near the hotel for your first northern lights attempt.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Keflavík Airport
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at Keflavík Airport Dunkin' or a petrol station sandwich (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (lobster rolls and sandwiches) on Laugavegur — filling and affordable (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Strætó bus card at the airport for cheaper local transport. Download the Vedur.is aurora forecast app immediately. January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C — layer up. Sunset is around 16:30 in January.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Reykjavík Flea Market (Kolaportið) if it's a weekend, or explore the old harbor area (Grandi district) on foot. Walk along the Sæbraut coastal path near the hotel for stunning winter sea views — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Sun Voyager sculpture (free) and walk to Harpa Concert Hall to admire the exterior architecture. Explore the National Museum of Iceland (1,800 ISK) to understand Icelandic history and culture on a rainy afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach near the hotel — a FREE outdoor geothermal hot pot area with warm seawater lagoon. Soak under the winter sky and watch for northern lights. Bring a towel and swimsuit.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — buy groceries at Bónus supermarket (budget chain) for bread, skyr, and fruit (~1,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's most famous hot dog stand near the harbor (~500 ISK for a hot dog with everything)
meals.dinner: Noodle Station on Laugavegur — hearty beef or vegetable noodle soup, very popular budget option (~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach is free in winter months (November–May). Always check opening hours before visiting. Stock up at Bónus or Krónan supermarkets for self-catering to save significantly on food costs.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Strætó bus toward the Reykjanes Peninsula. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates (free, ~500 ISK bus fare). Walk the dramatic volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon area — note: entry to the Blue Lagoon itself is expensive (~8,000–12,000 ISK). Instead, explore the surrounding Reykjanes volcanic landscape and lava fields for free. Visit the nearby Gunnuhver hot springs and mud pools (free geothermal area with dramatic steam vents).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. After dark (around 17:00 onward), join a FREE self-guided northern lights hunt. Drive or take a bus to Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) for an elevated dark viewing spot. Alternatively, the Grótta lighthouse peninsula near the hotel is excellent for aurora viewing with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — skyr with granola and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a self-made sandwich from supermarket groceries to eat on the Reykjanes Peninsula (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — multiple budget vendors under one roof, try the fish soup or lamb dishes (~2,000–3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Grótta Lighthouse peninsula is a 5-minute walk from the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront area — ideal for quick aurora checks without transportation costs. Always check tide times before walking to Grótta as it can flood.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car today for the famous Golden Circle route (car rental ~6,000–9,000 ISK/day for a small budget vehicle). Depart early (9:00) toward Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage site and another tectonic rift valley (free entry to the park).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: visit Geysir geothermal area to see the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes (free entry). Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls (free entry). Stunning even in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — the oldest swimming pool in Iceland and far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry). Soak in natural hot springs under the dark winter sky with northern lights potential. Return to Reykjavík.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the supermarket to eat at Gullfoss (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan on the return — surprisingly decent hot food options like soup and sandwiches (~1,500 ISK), or cook at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is the most cost-effective way to do the Golden Circle. Split costs with fellow travelers if possible. The Secret Lagoon is significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and more authentic. Total Golden Circle driving distance is approximately 230–300 km.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Perlan Museum on Öskjuhlíð hill — the 'Wonders of Iceland' exhibition includes a real ice cave tunnel (entry ~3,500 ISK, worth it for a rainy day). The building itself sits on geothermal hot water tanks and offers panoramic Reykjavík views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavík's free outdoor attractions: walk through Tjörnin pond area (often frozen in January, beautiful), visit the City Hall (free), and browse the colorful streets of the 101 district. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground Viking-age archaeological site (~2,200 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting evening: take a bus or walk to the Grótta lighthouse (5-minute walk from hotel). This is one of Reykjavík's best northern lights spots. Bring a thermos of hot tea, a tripod if you have one, and warm layers. Stay out 21:00–24:00 for best aurora window.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs and toast at accommodation
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food including rye bread with smoked trout or lamb (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty soup or pasta cooked at accommodation (~800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights in Iceland due to long dark nights (up to 19 hours of darkness). Check KP index on Vedur.is at 18:00 every evening to plan your night. KP-2 or above with clear skies is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip south along the Ring Road (rent a car or join a budget group tour ~8,000 ISK). Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall — you can walk behind the curtain of water (free, spectacular in winter with ice formations). Dress for getting wet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most iconic (free entry). Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views over the south coast. If conditions allow, walk the first section of the Fimmvörðuháls trail above the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and crashing Atlantic waves (free). Return to Reykjavík. Check aurora forecast — the South Coast drive offers dark skies away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack supermarket lunches — eat at Skógafoss car park with a view (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Skál! Craft Bar or a petrol station stop in Vík — Vík has a small N1 with hot food (~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: SAFETY WARNING: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves. Stay well back from the water — people have died here. Never turn your back on the ocean. January driving on Route 1 can be icy — check road conditions at road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and recover from active days. Visit the Reykjavík Botanic Garden (Grasagarðurinn) — free entry, beautiful even in winter with frost-covered plants and quiet walking paths near the hotel area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laugardalslaug — Reykjavík's largest public swimming pool and geothermal spa complex. Entry is only ~1,100 ISK and includes multiple hot pots, a steam room, and a large indoor/outdoor pool. Locals swim here year-round. An authentic Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's street art scene — the city has dozens of impressive murals throughout the 101 district (free walking tour). End the evening with a craft beer at Kaldi Bar (happy hour prices) or self-cater wine from the Vínbúðin state liquor store.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered leisurely breakfast — skyr, fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Mandi — Middle Eastern restaurant near Laugavegur, generous portions at low prices (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — buy lamb or fish from Bónus and cook at accommodation (~1,500 ISK for quality ingredients)

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug is the most authentic way to experience Icelandic hot pot culture at a fraction of tourist spa prices. Bring flip-flops and a towel. The etiquette requires showering thoroughly (without swimsuit) before entering the pools — follow the instructions posted.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car and head north toward Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours from Reykjavík). Stop at Deildartunguhver — Europe's most powerful hot spring (free to view, dramatic steam). Visit Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls (free, stunning lava-filtered waterfalls).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain (free). Drive through Snæfellsjökull National Park to the glacier volcano. Stop at Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) with dramatic rock formations and shipwreck remnants.
day_by_day.evening: Find a dark spot on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula for northern lights viewing — minimal light pollution here. The peninsula is one of Iceland's best aurora viewing locations. Drive back to Reykjavík or consider a budget guesthouse in Grundarfjörður (~6,000 ISK) to save driving time.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before 7:00 departure
meals.lunch: Pack supermarket picnic lunch to eat at Hraunfossar (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — local restaurant with fish soup and lamb (~3,000 ISK) or petrol station food (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day commitment from Reykjavík. Depart no later than 07:30 to maximize daylight hours (only about 5–6 hours of usable light in January). Road conditions can be challenging — check road.is. This peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' for its variety of landscapes.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight on Snæfellsnes, explore more of the peninsula in the morning — visit Arnarstapi coastal walk with dramatic sea cliffs and lava arches (free). Drive back toward Reykjavík via the Hvalfjörður tunnel or the scenic coastal route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavík by early afternoon. Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum (Árbæjarsafn) — a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses and buildings (~2,000 ISK). Alternatively, visit the Volcano House on Tryggvagata for an educational film about Icelandic volcanic eruptions (~2,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunting from Grótta lighthouse peninsula (walking distance from hotel). This is a dedicated aurora evening — pack hot drinks, warm layers, and plan to stay out 20:00–01:00 if conditions are favorable. January nights are long — maximize the opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or guesthouse breakfast on Snæfellsnes
meals.lunch: N1 petrol station stop on the drive back (~1,200 ISK for soup and sandwich)
meals.dinner: Cozy self-catered dinner at accommodation — buy fresh fish from Bónus and pan-fry with potatoes (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: After several active days, allow time for rest. The Grótta lighthouse is a 5-minute walk from the Aegean Bliss Resort — take advantage of this prime aurora location on clear nights. Set an aurora alarm on the Vedur app to alert you when KP index rises.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark — take a morning bus or drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula to explore the Seltún geothermal area (free). Colorful boiling mud pools, sulfur vents, and steaming ground make this a surreal landscape distinct from Gunnuhver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Krýsuvík lake area (Kleifarvatn) — a mysterious dark volcanic lake on the Reykjanes Peninsula (free). Walk the marked trail around the lake with views of volcanic craters. Stop at the Reykjanes lighthouse and the Viking World Museum in Njarðvík (~1,500 ISK) on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Visit the Reykjavík City Library (free, warm, great for budget travelers) or attend a free concert at Harpa Concert Hall lobby — free performances are sometimes scheduled in the public foyer. Check Harpa's website for schedule.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation
meals.lunch: Pack supermarket lunch for the Reykjanes Peninsula (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Soup Company (Súpan) on Laugavegur — excellent homemade soups with bread for ~1,800 ISK, very filling and warming

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is dramatically different from other parts of Iceland — very raw and volcanic. The entire peninsula sits on an active volcanic system. Recent eruptions (2021–2024 at Fagradalsfjall) have created new lava fields visible from the road — check if any safe viewing areas are accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to the Geothermal Exhibition at Hellisheiðarvirkjun power plant (approximately 20 minutes from Reykjavík on Route 1). Learn about Iceland's geothermal energy system (~1,500 ISK entry). The drive through the Hengill volcanic area is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hveragerði geothermal town — a small town where hot springs bubble up in gardens and greenhouses (free to walk around). Walk the Reykjadalur hot spring river trail — a 3 km hike to a naturally hot river where you can bathe (~free, just bring a swimsuit and towel). Trail can be icy in January — bring micro-spikes if available.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík for a final evening in the city center. Browse Laugavegur for budget souvenirs (avoid tourist shops — try the flea market or Kolaportið for cheaper finds). Final northern lights attempt from Grótta or Öskjuhlíð.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast
meals.lunch: Eat in Hveragerði at Ölverk Pizza & Brewery — surprisingly affordable wood-fired pizzas (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kebabinn on Laugavegur — large kebabs and wraps, very popular budget option (~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot river hike is FREE and one of Iceland's best budget hot spring experiences. The trail is approximately 6 km round trip and takes 2–3 hours. In January, start the hike by 12:00 to ensure you return before dark (sunset ~16:30). The hot river water temperature varies — test before submerging.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit favorite Reykjavík spots or explore anything missed. Visit the Imagine Peace Tower on Viðey Island (ferry from Skarfabakki harbor, ~1,500 ISK round trip) — John Lennon's memorial beacon, stunning in winter. The island also offers excellent aurora viewing away from city lights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laugardalslaug one final time for a long relaxing soak in the geothermal hot pots (~1,100 ISK). Pack and organize luggage for departure tomorrow. Buy any remaining Icelandic souvenirs — Bónus supermarket sells affordable Icelandic wool products, skyr, and local snacks to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights hunting night — this is your last chance. Head to Grótta lighthouse (walking distance from hotel) or take a short drive to Hafnarfjörður for darker skies. Stay out as late as possible if aurora activity is forecast. Celebrate the trip with a local Icelandic craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered special breakfast — treat yourself to smoked salmon on rye bread (Icelandic style)
meals.lunch: Fish Market area (Grandi) — Coocoo's Nest or Matur og Drykkur for a slightly splurge lunch to celebrate the trip (~3,500–4,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered farewell dinner at accommodation using remaining groceries, or Noodle Station for a comforting final meal (~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Check in online for your departure flight tonight if possible. Confirm Flybus shuttle booking for tomorrow's airport transfer. Leave a buffer of at least 3 hours before your flight departure time. Pack any liquid souvenirs (schnapps, fish products) in checked luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the Flybus shuttle from Reykjavík BSÍ terminal to Keflavík International Airport (~3,500 ISK). Allow 45 minutes for the journey plus 2.5–3 hours for airport check-in and security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, waterfalls, glaciers, and volcanic landscapes. Browse duty-free at Keflavík Airport for last-minute Icelandic spirits or chocolate (often cheaper than city shops).
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at connecting airport.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before checkout — use remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport food court — budget options available (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant at connecting hub

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days: Accommodation (pre-booked), Transport (~25,000 ISK bus + 2–3 car rental days), Food (~35,000–45,000 ISK self-catering mix), Attractions (~20,000–25,000 ISK), Hot Springs (~8,000 ISK), Miscellaneous (~10,000 ISK). Total estimate: ~100,000–115,000 ISK (~€680–€780 EUR) excluding flights and accommodation. January is low season — many attractions are less crowded and some offer winter discounts.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the dancing lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The signature experience includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask. Steam caves and a sauna enhance the relaxation while surrounded by dramatic lava fields.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers, offering a more intimate and local hot spring experience.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00 (Keflavík International Airport). Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Journey takes approximately 45–60 minutes depending on road conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearby shoreline to get your bearings. January daylight is very limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so enjoy the dusky coastal scenery and breathe in the crisp Arctic air.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the local main street, pop into a cozy café for a hot chocolate or Icelandic skyr dessert, then return to the resort for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Keflavík Airport (Pylsur hot dog stand or airport café) upon arrival – budget-friendly at ~1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local mid-range restaurant near the resort – try Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) or fish stew. Budget ~3,500–5,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30, so daylight is extremely limited. Keep expectations flexible for Day 1. Check the Aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) tonight – clear skies could mean northern lights from the resort beach.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a hearty breakfast at the resort. Then visit the nearby geothermal area on foot or by short drive – explore steaming vents, lava fields, and volcanic landscapes unique to Iceland's Reykjanes Peninsula. Many natural geothermal features are free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-book in advance – essential!). Soak in the iconic milky-blue silica-rich waters, enjoy the silica mud mask included in the Comfort package (~12,000–15,000 ISK). Allow 2–3 hours for a full experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort refreshed and glowing. After dinner, step outside or take a short drive away from artificial lights for your first dedicated northern lights watch. January offers long dark nights – prime aurora season.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby bakery – skyr with granola, fresh bread, and Icelandic butter
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or grab a smoothie/soup from their café bar (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby grill – grilled Arctic char or lamb burger (~4,000–6,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked online in advance – walk-ins are rarely accepted. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes for convenience. Bring a hair tie as the silica water can tangle hair.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus toward Reykjavík (approx. 45 min from Keflavík area). Spend the morning exploring Hallgrímskirkja Church (iconic tower with panoramic city views, ~1,000 ISK elevator fee), and the colorful streets of the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront – free to enter the lobby and admire the geometric glass architecture. Walk along the Sæbraut coastal path and spot the Sun Voyager sculpture. Browse the Kolaportið flea market if open (weekends only, free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Reykjavík's vibrant restaurant scene, then return to the resort. Before sleeping, check aurora forecasts – if KP index is 3+ and skies are clear, head to the beach for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík bakery stop – Brauð & Co. for fresh croissants and coffee (~1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur – Iceland's most famous hot dog stand, a Reykjavík institution (~500 ISK per hot dog)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Reykjavík restaurant – try Messinn for pan-fried fish of the day (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good day to visit Reykjavík as it is less crowded. Dress in very warm layers – January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C with wind chill making it feel much colder. Waterproof outer layers are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided Northern Lights Hunt Tour departing from the Reykjavík/Keflavík area in the early evening – but first, spend the morning at leisure. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) in Reykjavík, an underground museum built around a Viking longhouse (~2,200 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafnið) to learn about Icelandic history from settlement to modern times (~2,000 ISK). Stop at a local grocery store (Krónan or Bónus) to stock up on snacks and drinks for the aurora tour.
day_by_day.evening: Board the Northern Lights Hunt Tour minibus (~9,000–12,000 ISK per person). Expert guides drive away from light pollution into the dark Icelandic countryside, tracking clear skies in real time. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00. If clouds obscure the lights, most operators offer a free rebooking.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait and rye bread with smoked salmon at the resort
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja – traditional Icelandic flatbread with smoked trout (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the tour – Noodle Station in Reykjavík for hearty beef or vegetable noodle soup (~2,000 ISK, budget-friendly)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Northern Lights Hunt Tour in advance online. Wear your warmest clothing – standing outside in January nights can be -5°C to -10°C with wind. Tours usually provide blankets. Bring a tripod if you want aurora photos.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover after last night's late aurora tour. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Check aurora forecast for tonight and upcoming nights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Reykjanes Peninsula loop (approximately 2–3 hours including stops). Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free), the Gunnuhver hot spring geothermal area (free – dramatic boiling mud pools and steam vents), and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for dinner. If skies are clear, take an independent aurora watch from the resort beach – being beachfront gives an unobstructed dark horizon perfect for aurora spotting without light pollution from behind.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs, skyr, fresh fruit, and Icelandic rye bread
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from the grocery store eaten at a scenic viewpoint on the Reykjanes Peninsula drive
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort – Icelandic lamb shank or pan-fried cod (~4,500–6,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver hot springs are extremely powerful and dangerous – stay strictly on marked boardwalks. The Reykjanes Peninsula sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet – a geologically unique experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Golden Circle route (rent a car or join a guided day tour, ~15,000–20,000 ISK for guided). First stop: Þingvellir National Park – walk the Almannagjá rift valley between two tectonic plates (free entry, UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area – watch the mighty Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters high (free). Then visit Gullfoss Waterfall – one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic waterfalls, especially stunning with winter ice formations (free).
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the resort, stopping if aurora conditions are favorable. The Golden Circle area away from city lights is excellent for aurora viewing on the return drive.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant at the Geysir Center – traditional Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in a small town en route back, or resort dinner upon return (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route. In January, roads may be icy or snowy – drive cautiously and check road conditions on road.is before departing. Allow 8–10 hours for the full route with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest day. Sleep in, enjoy the resort facilities, and take a morning soak in the resort's hot tub or pool if available. Write postcards or journal about the trip so far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (~1.5 hours from the Keflavík area). Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891 – a natural hot spring in a rustic, atmospheric setting. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and more affordable (~3,500 ISK). Small geothermal geyser erupts every few minutes beside the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a quiet evening. Enjoy a relaxing dinner and an early night. Check aurora forecast – if conditions look promising, set an alarm for 22:00–01:00 for a beach aurora watch.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast – try Icelandic skyr with blueberry jam and oatmeal porridge
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Secret Lagoon's small café – soup and a sandwich (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cozy resort dinner – grilled salmon with Icelandic potatoes and butter sauce (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon water temperature is approximately 38–40°C year-round. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops (rentals available on-site). The drive to Flúðir passes through scenic rural Iceland – watch for Icelandic horses in roadside fields.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the South Coast of Iceland. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall – a stunning cascade you can walk behind (be cautious of ice in winter). Then visit nearby Gljúfrabúi, a hidden waterfall tucked inside a canyon (~2 hours from resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall – one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic falls. In winter, ice formations create dramatic rainbow-free but incredibly beautiful scenes. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast and Mýrdalsjökull glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive along the South Coast. Stop at the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík (if time permits) – dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks. Return to resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Skógafoss Café or packed lunch near the waterfalls (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort or a roadside restaurant – fish and chips or lamb stew (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: WARNING: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – never turn your back on the ocean. Stay well back from the water's edge. South Coast roads in January can be icy and subject to closure – always check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated aurora photography and planning morning. Sleep in after a long previous day. Review photos, charge camera batteries, and research aurora forecasting tools. Visit the local swimming pool (sundlaug) – every Icelandic town has a geothermally heated public pool (~1,000 ISK), a beloved local tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around the resort on foot or by car. Visit any nearby museums, art galleries, or craft shops. January is low season so many locals are more relaxed and welcoming to visitors. Pick up Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) at a local shop.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt Tour (if you booked a rebooking from Day 4, use it tonight, or book a fresh tour). Alternatively, drive independently to a dark spot – the resort's beachfront location is already excellent for aurora viewing if skies clear.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast or local bakery visit
meals.lunch: Local café or soup restaurant – kjötsúpa (lamb soup) is warming and traditional (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Early pre-tour dinner – hearty Icelandic meat dish or pasta at a mid-range restaurant (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January KP index forecasts: check en.vedur.is for aurora predictions. A KP of 2–3 is usually sufficient for viewing in Iceland away from city lights. The resort's beachfront position facing north is ideal for aurora watching.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2–2.5 hours from the Keflavík area). Visit the dramatic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano – made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Explore the lava fields and coastal scenery at the tip of the peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar villages on the Snæfellsnes south coast – dramatic basalt arch formations, sea caves, and birdlife. Walk the coastal path between the two villages (~2.5 km, 45 minutes). Stop at Kirkjufell mountain – Iceland's most photographed peak – for iconic winter shots.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is far from light pollution – if aurora conditions are favorable, pull over on the return drive for spectacular viewing with the glacier and mountain silhouettes as a backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the long drive north
meals.lunch: Café at Arnarstapi – fresh fish soup and bread with a view of the dramatic coastline (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort upon return – pizza or pasta for a lighter evening meal (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is a long day trip from the Keflavík area – depart by 08:30 to make the most of the limited daylight. Road 54 around the peninsula can be challenging in winter – a 4WD vehicle is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Reykjavík for a deeper city exploration. Visit the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland) – a stunning glass dome with exhibits on glaciers, volcanoes, and the northern lights, plus a real indoor ice cave (~4,900 ISK). Panoramic views of Reykjavík from the observation deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tjörnin city pond area and the City Hall. Visit the Ásmundarsafn sculpture museum (free in winter) and walk through the Laugardalur valley park. Stop at Laugardalslaug – Reykjavík's largest geothermal swimming complex with multiple hot pots (~1,200 ISK) for a mid-afternoon soak.
day_by_day.evening: Final Reykjavík evening – enjoy the city's vibrant food and nightlife scene. Walk along Laugavegur street, browse independent shops, and choose a memorable dinner restaurant for a mid-trip treat.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík brunch spot – Café Babalu for pancakes and coffee in a quirky, cozy setting (~2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall – Reykjavík's trendy food market with multiple vendors. Try Icelandic tacos or Asian-fusion (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at Grillmarkadurinn (Grill Market) – Icelandic ingredients with a modern twist, slightly splurge-worthy (~7,000–10,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug is extremely popular with locals and a genuine cultural experience. Bring a swimsuit and follow Icelandic pool etiquette – shower thoroughly without a swimsuit before entering the pools (this is mandatory, not optional).

day_by_day.morning: Final full day – relaxed morning at the resort. Enjoy a long breakfast, pack any items you won't need for the last night, and take a final sunrise walk along the beachfront (sunrise around 11:00 in January). Reflect on the trip and capture final photos of the resort and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a farewell soak if you wish (re-book online) or alternatively visit the Sky Lagoon in Kópavogur (~10,000–13,000 ISK) – a newer luxury geothermal spa with an infinity edge overlooking the ocean, closer to Reykjavík and very atmospheric in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Final aurora hunting opportunity. By now you know the best local dark spots. Head to the resort beach or a nearby dark hilltop with a flask of hot chocolate. If skies are clear, this is your last best chance for a memorable aurora display over the Atlantic Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory final full breakfast at the resort – order everything on the menu you haven't tried yet
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the lagoon or a packed picnic
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort – order the Icelandic tasting menu or chef's special if available (~5,000–8,000 ISK per person). Toast with Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps)

day_by_day.notes: If you haven't seen the northern lights yet, tonight is your last chance – statistically, January in Iceland offers aurora visibility on approximately 50–60% of clear nights. The resort's beachfront location facing north is one of the best possible positions for aurora viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last breakfast. If your flight is afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel and take a final short walk or visit a nearby café. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs – Icelandic sea salt, lava salt, lopapeysa wool goods, or skyr.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavík International Airport (45–60 minutes from the resort). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Keflavík duty-free is excellent for Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skincare products at competitive prices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry memories of geothermal hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and hopefully dancing green northern lights over the North Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a local bakery stop
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavík – Icelandic lamb sandwich or soup for a final taste of Iceland (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport duty-free opens before security in the departures hall – you can shop on the way in. The Blue Lagoon Skincare products are significantly cheaper here than in the lagoon itself. Confirm flight details and check for any January weather-related delays the night before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the dancing lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The signature experience includes access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and an algae mask. Steam caves and a sauna enhance the relaxation while surrounded by dramatic lava fields.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and small geysers, offering a more intimate and local hot spring experience.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and rich Viking heritage on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught Arctic char, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and colorful old harbor district.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Snuba Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Drift through the crystal-clear glacial waters of Silfra, the crack between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. With visibility exceeding 100 meters, this UNESCO World Heritage site offers a surreal underwater experience. Dry suits are provided, making it accessible even in cold temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing at Keflavík International Airport, a private luxury transfer awaits to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy complimentary welcome drinks and a resort orientation.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling into your beachfront suite, indulge in the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — conveniently located near Keflavík, it is a perfect first-day stop. Enjoy the signature silica mud mask, in-water massage, and premium algae mask ritual. Book the Retreat Spa package for exclusive access.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a leisurely dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Recover from travel fatigue with a curated Icelandic tasting menu featuring Arctic char, langoustine bisque, and skyr-based desserts paired with Icelandic craft spirits.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant — enjoy an elevated Icelandic lunch of smoked salmon, lamb flatbread, and fresh salads while overlooking the geothermal waters
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — 5-course Icelandic tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance as slots fill quickly. Request a geothermal-view suite upon check-in. January means very limited daylight (roughly 5–6 hours), so plan outdoor activities accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from central Reykjavik (short private transfer from resort). Explore the colorful old harbor, Hallgrímskirkja church, and sample traditional Icelandic bites including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, rye bread, and Brennivín schnapps with your expert local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland and the Harpa Concert Hall. Browse luxury Icelandic design boutiques along Laugavegur Street — pick up hand-knitted lopapeysa sweaters, volcanic salt sets, and artisan jewelry. Enjoy a private shopping consultation if arranged through the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt Tour — board a premium heated minibus with expert aurora guides. Head deep into the Reykjanes Peninsula countryside away from light pollution. Guides use real-time aurora forecasting apps and weather radar to maximize sighting chances. Hot cocoa and Icelandic pastries served en route.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet featuring Icelandic staples — skyr parfait, smoked lamb, fresh-baked rye bread, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant, Reykjavik — renowned for cast-iron pan-fried Arctic char and langoustine; a Reykjavik institution
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant; New Nordic cuisine using foraged and locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tours are weather-dependent. The tour operator will confirm departure based on cloud cover forecasts. January offers some of Iceland's best aurora probability (KP index permitting). Dress in thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Golden Circle tour — depart early to maximize the brief daylight window. Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site), walk the rift valley between tectonic plates, and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: witness the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir Geothermal Area (erupts every 5–10 minutes), then marvel at the thundering Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January for a dramatic ice-laced spectacle. Warm up with Icelandic lamb soup at a nearby farmhouse café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite hot tub session under the stars with aurora watch — your butler will alert you if the northern lights become visible. Opt for a relaxing couples' spa treatment at the resort wellness center.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — grab-and-go luxury packed breakfast box arranged by the concierge for the early departure
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Geysir — dine inside a working tomato greenhouse; famous for tomato soup, tomato-based cocktails, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: In-resort dining — private beachfront table with a curated seafood menu featuring Icelandic lobster tail, pan-seared cod, and volcanic stone dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 in January. Time outdoor stops carefully to catch the best light at Gullfoss and Þingvellir. Private guiding ensures flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Snuba Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir — experience the awe-inspiring crack between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Drift through some of the world's clearest glacial water with visibility exceeding 100 meters. Dry suits are provided; no prior diving experience needed for snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this natural hot spring offers an intimate, authentic soak surrounded by bubbling geothermal vents and a small geyser. January steam creates a magical, ethereal atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt Tour — second attempt for optimal aurora viewing. Tonight's tour heads toward the Haukadalur valley area for darker skies. Guides set up tripods for complimentary aurora photography assistance. Warm Icelandic lamb stew served in thermoses.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, Icelandic flatbread, and fresh berry smoothies
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch provided by the resort in a luxury insulated hamper — consumed at the Secret Lagoon's cozy indoor warming hut
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik — celebrated restaurant serving modern interpretations of historical Icelandic recipes; try the cod's head and lamb neck

day_by_day.notes: Silfra water temperature is 2–4°C year-round — dry suits keep you warm but fingers and face will feel the cold. The experience lasts approximately 3 hours including briefing. Book well in advance for this exclusive slot.

day_by_day.morning: Private South Coast tour begins — depart for the dramatic South Shore. Stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall (walkable behind the curtain of water — icy and magical in January with frozen formations) and Skógafoss waterfall with its legendary hidden treasure chest folklore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach — one of the world's most stunning beaches with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and thunderous Atlantic waves. Visit the black-sand dunes and the Reynisfjall mountain cave formations. Drive on to Vík village for a brief exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a pre-arranged overnight luxury stay at a South Coast boutique lodge (or return to Aegean Bliss Resort via private transfer if preferred). Enjoy a private chef-prepared dinner featuring local South Iceland lamb and glacier-fed river trout.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — Icelandic oatmeal with bilberries, smoked meats, and artisan cheeses
meals.lunch: Skál! Craft Beer & Food in Vík — hearty Icelandic lamb burger and local craft beers in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at lodge or resort — slow-roasted South Iceland lamb shank, root vegetable gratin, and Icelandic cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara Beach has dangerous sneaker waves — always keep a safe distance from the shoreline and heed all warning signs. January ice can make the walk behind Seljalandsfoss extremely slippery; microspikes recommended (provided by guide).

day_by_day.morning: Glacier hiking on Sólheimajökull glacier — a dramatic outlet glacier of the mighty Mýrdalsjökull ice cap. Strap on crampons and explore crevasses, ice caves, and blue ice formations with a certified glacier guide. The contrast of black ash and blue ice is visually extraordinary in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic landscapes. Watch enormous icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift through the lagoon. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating a surreal ice-sculpture landscape. Walk to Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora watch from Jökulsárlón — the glacier lagoon is one of Iceland's premier northern lights viewing spots, with ice reflections doubling the spectacle. Your private guide sets up aurora photography. Return to resort or overnight at a nearby luxury guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box from resort or lodge
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Glacier Café — warm lamb soup and fresh-baked scones with Icelandic butter
meals.dinner: Hótel Skaftá or similar South Iceland luxury property — pan-seared Arctic char with pickled vegetables and brown butter, followed by skyr cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately a 4.5-hour drive from Reykjavik — this is a long but spectacular day. A private driver/guide is essential. Glacier hiking requires moderate fitness. All gear provided by the glacier guide company.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Skaftafell Nature Reserve within Vatnajökull National Park — explore ice cave formations within the glacier. A private ice cave tour takes you into electric-blue crystal ice caves accessible only in winter months (November–March). These caves are among Iceland's most breathtaking natural wonders.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back westward along the Ring Road, stopping at Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon — a stunning 2-kilometer-long, 100-meter-deep canyon with winding river below. Also stop at Systrafoss waterfall near Kirkjubæjarklaustur. Enjoy the dramatic winter light casting long golden shadows across the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a restorative evening with a full spa treatment — volcanic mud wrap, hot stone massage, and geothermal pool soak at the resort wellness center. Early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at overnight lodge or a luxury packed box en route
meals.lunch: Roadside luxury picnic prepared by your guide — Icelandic lamb sandwiches on rye, pickled herring, skyr pots, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Resort in-room private dining — truffle-glazed cod, lobster bisque, and warm Icelandic lava cake with bilberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Ice caves are a seasonal highlight and must be booked through certified guides — never enter independently. Cave accessibility depends on glacier conditions; your guide will confirm the safest and most spectacular cave for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely spa breakfast. Take a private yoga or meditation session arranged by the resort overlooking the beachfront. Alternatively, enjoy a private geothermal pool session at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (walk across the gap between tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (Iceland's largest geothermal area), and the dramatic Reykjanestá lighthouse at Iceland's southwestern tip. The rugged lava fields are otherworldly in January.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt Tour — third opportunity for aurora viewing, this time along the Reykjanes Peninsula coastline for minimal light pollution and dramatic ocean backdrops. Champagne and canapés served during the wait.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — full Icelandic spread with smoked lamb, pickled herring, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Bryggjan Brugghús Brewery in Grindavík — craft beer tasting paired with lobster soup and open-faced sandwiches
meals.dinner: Tjöruhúsið, Reykjavik — legendary fish restaurant serving daily-catch seafood in communal pots; an authentic Reykjavik institution

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver mud pools are extremely hot and active — stay on marked paths at all times. The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically active; your guide will provide safety briefings. January aurora probability remains high on clear nights.

day_by_day.morning: Private whale watching tour from Reykjavik Old Harbour (winter season offers humpback and minke whale sightings, plus white-beaked dolphins). Board a premium heated vessel with panoramic windows and an onboard marine biologist guide. Hot drinks and fresh pastries served aboard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition — the world's largest whale exhibition with life-size models. Then explore the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús) and the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin), built around a Viking-age longhouse excavation. Private curator-guided tour available.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private northern lights flight — a luxury small-plane aurora tour that flies above the cloud cover to guarantee northern lights viewing regardless of ground weather. A truly once-in-a-lifetime premium experience. Land back at Reykjavik domestic airport and transfer to resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked salmon Benedict, Icelandic yogurt with honey, and freshly squeezed Arctic berry juice
meals.lunch: Kopar Restaurant at Reykjavik Old Harbour — seafood-forward menu with panoramic harbor views; try the langoustine tails and lobster bisque
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — ultra-exclusive 12-seat counter restaurant with a theatrical chef's tasting menu; one of Iceland's most coveted dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: The private northern lights flight is a premium add-on (approximately €500–800 per person) but guarantees aurora viewing above clouds — ideal insurance for cloudy January nights. Book months in advance as seats are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile adventure on Langjökull glacier — Iceland's second-largest glacier. A private helicopter transfer from Reykjavik to the glacier (approximately 20 minutes) provides breathtaking aerial views of Iceland's interior highlands blanketed in snow. Snowmobile across the vast white expanse with a certified guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Into the Glacier — explore the man-made ice tunnel system inside Langjökull glacier. Walk through illuminated blue ice chambers, a chapel carved into the ice, and learn about Iceland's glacial geology. A truly extraordinary subterranean ice world experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private helicopter or luxury vehicle. Indulge in a premium hot spring evening — arrange a private geothermal pool experience at the resort or a nearby exclusive hot spring. Stargazing and aurora watch from the heated pool.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Packed luxury lunch box consumed inside the glacier tunnel system — a uniquely memorable dining setting
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market), Reykjavik — Iceland's finest grill restaurant featuring dry-aged Icelandic beef, reindeer, and puffin; excellent wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter transfer is weather-dependent. Snowmobiling requires a valid driver's license. All safety gear and thermal suits are provided. The glacier experience is physically accessible for most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed resort morning — private sunrise photography walk along the beachfront with a professional photographer guide. Capture Iceland's dramatic winter coastline, sea ice formations, and the resort in the soft golden-hour light (sunrise approximately 11:00 in January).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn on the Golden Circle route — a boutique geothermal spa with three naturally heated pools, steam rooms built directly over geothermal vents, and a traditional Icelandic rye bread baking demonstration (bread baked underground using geothermal heat). Far more intimate than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt Tour — dedicated aurora photography night with a professional astrophotographer guide. Learn long-exposure techniques and leave with stunning aurora images. Celebrate potential sightings with Icelandic schnapps and gourmet canapés under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Icelandic spread with emphasis on local dairy, fresh-baked goods, and smoked fish platters
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant, Laugarvatn — elegant lakeside dining featuring locally foraged ingredients; try the Arctic char from the lake and homemade geothermal rye bread
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron), Reykjavik — legendary lobster soup shack beloved by locals and gourmands alike; followed by a nightcap at Slippbarinn cocktail bar

day_by_day.notes: Fontana Geothermal Baths requires advance booking for private sessions. The rye bread baking demonstration is a uniquely Icelandic cultural experience not to be missed. January offers excellent aurora probability on clear nights.

day_by_day.morning: Private horse riding tour on Icelandic horses — these unique, small, and incredibly sure-footed horses are a national treasure. Ride through lava fields and along the coastline near the resort. The Icelandic horse's exclusive tölt gait provides an unusually smooth ride even for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum in Reykjavik — built atop six geothermal hot water tanks, it features an immersive northern lights planetarium show, a real indoor ice cave, and exhibitions on Iceland's natural wonders. The glass dome observation deck offers 360° views over Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner at the resort — arrange a private chef's table experience or a beachfront candlelit dinner with a sommelier-curated wine pairing. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days in Iceland over a multi-course celebration meal.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon, Icelandic caviar, freshly baked pastries, and seasonal fruit with Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Perlan Café with panoramic views — light Icelandic lunch of fish soup, open-faced sandwiches, and skyr desserts
meals.dinner: Private resort chef's table — 7-course bespoke Icelandic tasting menu with paired Icelandic gins, schnapps, and international wines; personalized menu card as a keepsake

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic horse riding is suitable for all experience levels. The horses are gentle and responsive. Helmets and riding gear are provided. The Perlan northern lights show runs multiple times daily — book the premium immersive dome experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast with panoramic beachfront views. Pack and check out at leisure. Arrange a final short soak in the resort's private geothermal pool before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. En route, make a final stop at the Blue Lagoon's Retreat Spa for a 2-hour farewell soak and spa treatment — the ultimate send-off. The Retreat Spa offers a private, exclusive section away from the main lagoon crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories, a camera full of aurora photographs, and a deep appreciation for the land of fire and ice. Airport lounge access arranged; enjoy complimentary Icelandic snacks and duty-free shopping for local spirits, volcanic salt, and Icelandic skincare products.

meals.breakfast: Grand final resort breakfast — full à la carte service with every Icelandic specialty sampled over 13 days
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Retreat Restaurant — exclusive in-water dining service with floating tray; enjoy langoustine, smoked salmon, and sparkling wine while soaking
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or on-board dining

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa requires advance booking and is priced separately from the main lagoon. Allow at least 2.5 hours at the lagoon before needing to depart for the airport (30-minute drive to Keflavík). Duty-free in Iceland is excellent — stock up on Brennivín, Icelandic gin, and volcanic salt flakes.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026
